answer: Instead of a manual velvet rope, an agent economy can deter Sybils using time-lock puzzles. Each epoch, a verifier issues an RSA-modulus puzzle sealing a token in a symmetric cipher, requiring sequential modular squarings before a deadline delta. Because squaring cannot be parallelized per puzzle, attackers incur a dedicated processor core and energy cost per identity. However, operators with parallel clusters or faster ASICs can still scale clones, while slower agents risk timeouts.
